proposal.hypothesis: LiCaAlF6 is a wide-gap mixed fluoride whose Li, Ca and Al cations are all highly oxidation-resistant and reduction-resistant. Compared with binary LiF, the Al3+ and Ca2+ framework may suppress the S-, Cl- and P-containing reduction products (SCl, S, LiPF6) seen at the sulfide contact. It is a halide with no P-O, S-O or O2- species, so it should avoid the large oxide-contact penalties.

The remaining candidates in the halide family are fluorides, so LiCaAlF6 is the closest untested halide with a different cation set.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2SiF6 is a wide-gap fluoride whose Si4+ cation is hard to reduce, like the Al3+ and Ca2+ framework of LiCaAlF6. Its F- anion avoids the P-O, S-O and O2- products that drove the oxide penalties. Compared with binary LiF, which gave a penalty of 0.310, a high-valence, reduction-resistant cation in the fluoride framework should suppress the S- and P-containing reduction products.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2TiF6 is a wide-gap fluoride with a hard, high-valence Ti4+ center, the same structural family as Li2SiF6 (penalty 0.081) and the mixed LiCaAlF6 (penalty 0.048, the only acceptable result so far). Its F- framework avoids the P-O, S-O and O2- products that drove the oxide and phosphate penalties. Ti4+ is somewhat easier to reduce than Si4+, so this tests whether a transition-metal fluoride keeps the low contact penalty while staying insulating.
